sam (support): Customer ACME reports sudden p99 jump for text-generation endpoint ~15:03 UTC. p99 from ~350ms -> ~3.1s, p95 ~800ms. No error spikes, just long tail. Happening across 3 zones. Repro curl: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -s -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n'`
jordan (oncall): looking at infra metrics now. I see ingress queue depth climb ~14:58 -> 15:05, backlog ~1.2k requests. Worker pod CPU steady but threads all busy. Admission control started kicking at 500 concurrent but backlog kept growing.
mira (eng-runtime): thanks. Any recent config or rollout? Also which model and batch settings? Could be batching/caching interaction causing head-of-line waits.
sam (support): Customer using model rwd-llama-13b, batch_size=32, max_tokens=512. No rollout on our side in last 24h per deploy bot. They reported burst of parallel requests from a customer job.
jordan (oncall): attaching quick logs for the ingress router (excerpt): ```[2026-03-16T15:00:12Z] conn=... queue_depth=1200 admit=false reason=concurrency_limit
[2026-03-16T15:01:03Z] worker-23 accept=0 active=48 queued=240
[2026-03-16T15:02:45Z] router drop_ratio=0.12 backlog=980``` Looks like admission threshold stalled; fallback to queueing rather than fast-fail.
mira (eng-runtime): I think the admission controller predicate didn't fast-fail because we have `allow_queueing=true` for tenant ACME. That defers failures but creates long tails. Two mitigations: 1) temporarily set allow_queueing=false for tenant to fast-fail and relieve worker pileup; 2) spin up more dedicated worker replicas for rwd-llama-13b or reduce batch_size to lower latency.
alex (customer-success): I can ask ACME to toggle client-side concurrency or throttle spikes, but prefer platform fix first. They need low tail latency for production traffic.
jordan (oncall): I can flip allow_queueing=false for that tenant for the next 10m as an emergency measure. Any objections?
mira (eng-runtime): Do it. Also push a 5m config that reduces default batch_size to 16 for that model on the tenant until we stabilize. We'll monitor KV cache hitrate — if many short requests, smaller batches help.
sam (support): made the change to allow_queueing=false for tenant acme-42 at 15:08 UTC.
devbot: config-change: tenant=acme-42 changed allow_queueing=false by sam (support) at 2026-03-16T15:08:02Z
jordan (oncall): immediate improvement in metrics: backlog dropped from ~1100 -> ~40 within 90s, p99 sliding down to ~420ms. p95 now ~280ms. Marking mitigation successful but not root-cause.
mira (eng-runtime): next steps for root cause: 1) collect full request traces for 14:50-15:10 window; 2) run model profiling on worker pods to check for lock contention on KV cache or GC pauses; 3) review admission controller logic that gates queueing favoring silent queue instead of fast-fail when thresholds cross quickly.
sam (support): asked customer to reduce peak parallel runs and sent repro curl. They can also roll back to client-side backoff immediately.
alex (customer-success): ACME confirms tail improved after your change and will implement client-side backoff in the short term.
jordan (oncall): raising ENG-RUNTIME ticket ENGRT-4826, assigned to mira, priority P1 for investigation and a followup patch to admission controller to prefer controlled fast-fail under sustained rise. I'll also add a runbook note about toggling allow_queueing per-tenant for oncall.
mira (eng-runtime): ACK. I'll collect traces and attach a small reproducer script. Tentative root-cause hypothesis: admission controller hysteresis + large batch sizes + tenant-level allow_queueing created unbounded queueing under sudden burst. Plan: repro in staging, add a short-circuit fast-fail when queue_growth_rate > threshold, and add metrics/alert for queue_growth_rate.
sam (support): thanks all. I'll close the support escalation and keep the customer updated.
